reviewType: Independent final product-cut review; read-only production scope

decision.scope: KEEP is a selection recommendation for these exact bytes. It does not lock a post, approve spending/voice, select an account/time or make the held earlier films publishable.

whyKeep: The recognizable marinated chicken, reflective foil and kitchen depth are materially stronger than the held orange-nugget primitive film. Food dominates the frame instead of becoming a small insert on an empty card.
A sheet entering the one oven while another waits makes the capacity story visible before the app proof; the video is relevant to the method claim rather than unrelated preparation footage.
The genuine app interaction reaches Dairy-Free and six servings, then the real endpoint is held. This is readable at 390px and fixes the earlier risk of ending on an intermediate setting.
The large exact method excerpt links the recorded adaptation to the visible plan. The CTA follows a compact action → setting → method sequence rather than several long fact slides.

actualObservedTimeline.event: Food and foil fill the stage while Two more for dinner? poses a concrete scaling problem. Native motion appears immediately; no empty semantic opening.
Same oven. Two sheets. accompanies one sheet entering the oven while another remains outside. The tray moves without a human hand and is visibly synthetic planning illustration.
Actual RecipeFix modal changes Dairy-Free and servings through intermediate states. Intermediate five is valid action, not the endpoint claim.
Genuine captured endpoint holds selected Dairy-Free and 6 servings. Both the six-serving label and numeric 6 control are visible in actual 390px samples.
The method changes, too. plus actual source pixels broil one sheet at a time. Large enough to read at phone scale; no paragraph scroll.
Make your recipe fit. and recipefix.app close over the same kitchen world. The 2.5s static ending is a normal CTA hold, not another lengthy explanatory scene.

sourceEndpoint.scope: Historical combined Dairy-Free 4→6 response, recorded Oct 21, 2026; not a fresh inference or filmed cooked/tasted result. Disclosure states recorded result and AI planning illustration. No nutrition number or appliance-detection claim observed.
sourceEndpoint.methodPhrase: broil one sheet at a time

clippingAndCopy.mainProof: Dairy-Free controls, six-serving label/number, method phrase and CTA are not clipped and are readable at 390px. Copy stays concise.
clippingAndCopy.minorCropIssue: The lower Adapt recipe button is partially cropped by the UI card mask. It looks less finished than a clean card boundary, but the claimed six-serving proof is intact. This is a minor crop/craft defect rather than a reason to discard the whole candidate.
clippingAndCopy.scopeNote: This review did not operate the published app or prove a new adaptation. The actual export was inspected, not just its component source.

remainingTasteLimits: The self-propelled/hovering tray remains an obvious synthetic cue. Keep the planning-illustration disclosure; do not call this authentic kitchen footage or a physically cooked result.

This is a conventional compact product-ad structure, not an exceptional entertainment film. It is stronger enough to keep for founder selection, without claiming the audience will watch, like or convert.
Source/disclosure footer is legible in the native and 390px samples; actual TikTok/Instagram overlay placement was not tested.
